# v3.00

**Nothing in the application changes in this release.** If you are coming from
v2.99, no feature, screen, setting or stored data is different, and there is
nothing to do on upgrade beyond the usual update.

It rolls up a single dev pre-release, **v3.00-dev**.

## Why the number went from 2.99 to 3.00

**This is not a major release, despite how it looks.** Version numbers here move
one step per change: the part after the dot counts 00 to 99, and then the part
before the dot goes up by one. 2.99 was simply the last number before that
happened.

So v3.00 means "one step after v2.99" and nothing else. It is not a new
generation of the product, there is no migration, and no behaviour has been
redesigned. Treat it exactly as you would have treated a v2.100 had the numbering
worked that way — which, as it turns out, is the whole story of this release.

## Fixed

- **The automated release check no longer blocks a correct version at the
  rollover.** This is a change to the project's own build process rather than to
  the product. One of the checks that runs before a release verifies the version
  moved by exactly one step; it compared numbers in a way that was correct
  everywhere except at this boundary, where it would have refused the correct
  3.00 and accepted an invalid number instead. It now understands the rollover,
  and rejects a malformed version with an explanation.

  How your system finds and installs updates was never affected by this — that
  comparison had 3.00 right all along. Only the internal release check was wrong.

## Upgrading

No action needed, and nothing to reconfigure. **If you have update automation or
monitoring that treats a change in the first number as significant, this is the
release to tell it about** — the jump is cosmetic, not structural.

## Still current from v2.99

v2.99 was a security and hardening release covering permission changes taking
effect immediately, company-scoped visibility, and what leaves the system in
exported files. If you have not taken v2.99 yet, this release includes all of it,
and **updating promptly is recommended.**
